guarantees.claim: On reset (rst_ni low), sw_cmd_o is set to CmdNone.
When not in reset and block_swcmd is low, sw_cmd_o is driven to sw_cmd_i on the rising edge of clk_i.
When not in reset and block_swcmd is high, sw_cmd_o holds its previous value.

assumptions.claim: sw_cmd_i must be stable around the rising edge of clk_i to avoid metastability or data corruption when block_swcmd is low.
assumptions.cond: block_swcmd == 0 at the positive clock edge
assumptions.risk: Unstable input may cause meta-stability or incorrect command capture.

uncertain_points.claim: block_swcmd is driven externally; if it remains high after reset, sw_cmd_o will never update and the KMAC may starve for commands.
No validation of sw_cmd_i (range, parity, integrity) is performed; an invalid command is passed directly to sw_cmd_o and subsequently to the command processing logic.
uncertain_points.cond: sw_cmd_i carries an illegal or corrupted command value
uncertain_points.risk: Security-critical command misinterpretation or system state corruption in the KMAC engine.

uncertain_points.claim: If block_swcmd is deasserted for only a single cycle, a glitch or temporary value on sw_cmd_i could be captured as a valid command.
uncertain_points.cond: block_swcmd low exactly one clock cycle
uncertain_points.risk: Spurious command execution due to a transient input value.
